Update from tracing:
- KV cache miss rate for FastDesk traffic jumped from 6% -> 27% during the window (17:10–17:50). Eviction counters show sustained high churn on hosts in cluster west-3.
- There is a correlation with longer chat histories (avg seq len +35%), which pushes more KV pages into working set and increases memory pressure.
- No clear kernel oom kills or GC pauses. CPU utilization spiky, network retransmits slightly elevated.

Recommendation: temporary config change to increase KV cache size for the FastDesk tenant (applied to their shard group) + enable LRU prefetch for tokens we see commonly. This is lower risk than model fallback and should reduce p99 inside 10–20 mins.

I'll apply a conservative cache bump and monitor. If we don't see p99 drop under 700ms for canary in 18m, we should route all traffic to the burst pool and consider a model downgrade.

-Rachel
Lead SRE, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: Chat connections failing + huge delays during evening peak

Infra tracing findings:
- Socket accept backlog peaked and we saw file descriptor pressure on the front-line proxies at ~17:20–17:30. Several hosts hit ephemeral port exhaustion due to rapid reconnects from mobile clients.
- Kernel TCP retransmit rate increased 12x but no packet drops on the hypervisor network fabric.

Mitigations applied at 18:25: 
- Increased ephemeral port range and reduced TCP TIME_WAIT reuse for front-line proxies.
- Backpressure applied at the load balancer to smooth accepts (the LB will queue and reject aggressively rather than let user agents retry immediately).

Result: by 18:32 PST we see p99 for canary traffic ~540ms, overall p99 trending down to ~800–900ms. Still slightly above baseline; monitoring for a full hour.

-Aditya
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
